title: Nia's Hidden Frog
markdown:
Nia loved her sun-drenched garden, and so did her fluffy grey cat, Wisp. Wisp’s eyes were soft emeralds. His paws were as gentle as mist. Today they played with Nia’s favourite toy: a little green frog, smooth like a river stone warmed by the sun.

“Ribbit, ribbit,” Nia whispered, making it hop near the tall whispering reeds by the gently flowing stream. Wisp watched, tail swaying slow, a sleepy branch in a soft breeze. Then Nia sent the frog a little too far. It landed by the water’s edge and seemed to melt away.

“Where did it go?” She peered into rustling green stems. Wisp padded closer, sniffing with curious whiskers. The reeds were a lovely green, just like the frog.

Dr Sol ambled over, footsteps a soft rustle. “Hello, my little explorers. What’s amiss?”

“My green frog toy has vanished in the reeds.”

He knelt, voice a calm murmur. “An interesting puzzle. Look at Wisp.” Wisp, grey fur, had nested near a patch of greyish-green moss. A fluffy shadow in the dappled light. He looked as if he belonged there.

“It’s like he’s wearing the same clothes as where he’s sitting,” Nia said.

Sol nodded. “Nature uses colours to help living things blend in, to rest safely. The trick is called camouflage. Your green frog, the same colour as these green reeds, is playing a hiding game.”

Nia’s mind buzzed, but quietly, the bedtime sort of buzz. “So if the frog is green and the reeds are green, he might be hiding in the green, and we can’t spot him because he looks like everything else?”

“Precisely.” A chuckle like tumbling pebbles. “Look very carefully, very gently, among the greenest parts. Wisp’s sharp eyes might help.”

They moved closer. Nia felt the cool smooth stems. Wisp let out a soft Mrow? and tilted his head, emerald gaze fixed. His nose pointed at a clump of particularly tall lush reeds. Nia followed. There, peeking from behind a broad green leaf, was the smooth green toy frog. Blended in so perfectly.

“You found him.”

Nia held him close. “He was the same colour as the reeds. Camouflage.”

Sol’s gaze swept the garden. He did not pile on a lecture about ladybirds’ bright shells, which are a different kind of clever. The moss and the reeds were enough.

Nia hugged the frog, smooth and cool. Wisp purred, a tiny contented motor. The garden quieted in fading light. Shy stars began. Nia yawned a big sleepy yawn. Good to know how things could hide. Better to know the frog was safe beside her. Soon, tucked in her warm bed, Wisp at her feet, she drifted off, mind as peaceful as the sleeping garden, one green secret already found.
characters: Nia (a curious gardener), Wisp (a cat), Sol (a scientist)
author: StoryGen Community
